question: What organ performs oxygen exchange for the growing foetus?

options.A: The kidneys
options.B: The liver
options.C: The placenta
options.D: The foetal lungs

explanation: Because the lungs are not yet breathing air, the placenta takes over the job of bringing in oxygen and removing waste. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h1)

question: A community health nurse organizes a blood pressure screening in the marketplace. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Terminal prevention

explanation: Screenings are classified as secondary prevention because they catch health problems early when treatment is most effective. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h3)

question: If a factory worker's liver enzymes are overactive due to chemical exposure, what usually happens to their regular medications?

options.A: The drugs will instantly crystallize inside the stomach lining
options.B: The drugs will turn into harmless vitamins inside the bloodstream
options.C: The drugs will remain active inside the body for many extra weeks
options.D: The drugs may break down too fast and lose their therapeutic effect

explanation: When liver enzymes are in overdrive, they clear out medications too quickly. This means the drug leaves the body before it even has a chance to help the patient! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T10#GNS125_U5_T10_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard precaution practice?

options.A: Using a private negative-pressure room for every patient
options.B: Performing hand hygiene before and after patient contact
options.C: Using safe injection practices and proper sharps disposal
options.D: Wearing gloves when touching non-intact skin or body fluids

explanation: Negative-pressure rooms are special transmission-based precautions for airborne germs, not a routine standard precaution for everyone. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h6)

question: A patient's forehead temperature reads 37.8°C, but they look pale and are shivering hard. What should you suspect?

options.A: The patient has a severe brain injury
options.B: Shivering can make skin feel cold while a real fever is hiding underneath
options.C: The thermometer is definitely broken and should be thrown away
options.D: The patient has no fever at all and needs no more checks

explanation: When shivering causes surface blood vessels to tighten up, skin readings can look normal or low even when core temperature is climbing. Always keep a close eye!

question: Why should a nurse avoid abruptly stopping a patient's compulsive ritual?

options.A: It immediately destroys the therapeutic trust built with the doctor
options.B: It breaks hospital legal regulations regarding patient property rights
options.C: It causes permanent physical paralysis in the patient's limbs
options.D: It triggers severe panic and dangerous anxiety spikes in the patient

explanation: Correct! Compulsions are their current shield against panic; snatching that away suddenly throws them into massive distress.

question: What is a major financial barrier for families of special children in Nigeria?

options.A: Mandatory free private nursing care at home
options.B: Excessive government funding for all childhood treatments
options.C: Free international travel for medical checkups
options.D: High out-of-pocket costs for therapies and medical supplies

explanation: Most families bear the financial burden of care directly because public insurance coverage for chronic disabilities is limited. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h8)

question: If a patient suddenly cannot move their leg due to a spinal injury, which part of the spinal grey matter is likely damaged?

options.A: Dorsal horn
options.B: Lateral horn
options.C: Central canal
options.D: Ventral horn

explanation: Think of the ventral (front) horn as the exit route for movement. It houses the motor neuron cell bodies that send direct signals to your skeletal muscles to make them move.

question: What is the job of transferrin in the body?

options.A: It filters water-soluble vitamins out of the blood for renal excretion.
options.B: It acts as a transport protein that carries iron through the bloodstream.
options.C: It stores excess calcium inside the dense matrix of long bones.
options.D: It produces active vitamin D inside the cells of the renal cortex.

explanation: Think of transferrin as a dedicated taxi in your blood plasma. Its sole job is to pick up iron and safely drive it to places like your bone marrow!

question: What is the best feeding item to use when giving ORS to an infant?

options.A: A clean cup and spoon
options.B: A rubber feeding bottle
options.C: A wide-spout drinking straw
options.D: A plastic syringe with a needle

explanation: Always choose a clean cup and spoon! Baby bottles have narrow parts that are very hard to clean properly and can easily trap germs that cause more infections.

question: What happened when major scandals broke out about ships dumping toxic waste?

options.A: They forced world leaders to create a binding international waste treaty
options.B: They led to a complete ban on all maritime shipping worldwide
options.C: They encouraged developing nations to build more local incinerators
options.D: They proved that ocean water naturally neutralizes heavy metal toxins

explanation: Well done! When media and the public saw wandering ships dumping dangerous cargo, world leaders realized they had to step in with strict international rules.

question: Why is it smart to check a menu for a nice mix of colors, textures, and flavors?

options.A: It guarantees that the food will require zero cooking preparation time
options.B: It stimulates appetite and makes the meal more enjoyable to eat
options.C: It prevents the kitchen staff from having to wash dishes afterwards
options.D: It ensures that every food item tastes exactly the same

explanation: Nobody wants a boring, pale plate! Colorful, well-textured food makes patients actually want to eat.

question: In global polio campaigns, what does the abbreviation 'AFP' stand for?

options.A: Asymmetrical Facial Palsy
options.B: Active Fever Protocol
options.C: Advanced Functional Pathology
options.D: Acute Flaccid Paralysis

explanation: You're doing great! AFP stands for acute flaccid paralysis—the key sign health workers watch out for to catch hidden polio cases early.

question: What is the main feature of a Type A adverse drug reaction?

options.A: It is predictable and depends on the size of the dose.
options.B: It never goes away even if the drug is stopped immediately.
options.C: It only happens to patients with weak immune systems.
options.D: It is completely unpredictable and has nothing to do with the dose.

explanation: Type A reactions are basically an exaggerated normal effect of the medication. Because of this, they are dose-dependent and easier to predict!

question: How is the best way to kick off the discussion section?

options.A: By summarizing the primary findings in plain language
options.B: By proposing a brand new theory of human behavior
options.C: By listing every single p-value calculated in the study
options.D: By criticizing the work done by previous authors

explanation: Spot on! Starting with a clear, simple summary reminds your reader of the main scoop before you dive deep into what it all means.

question: Which of the following is NOT a common cause of rectovaginal fistula?

options.A: Obstetric trauma during difficult childbirth
options.B: Normal spontaneous vaginal delivery without tears
options.C: Inflammatory bowel diseases like Crohn's
options.D: Surgical complications from perineal repair

explanation: An uncomplicated, normal delivery does not cause the severe tissue damage necessary to create a rectovaginal fistula. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h3)

question: Why does a malnourished patient usually take longer to recover from an infection?

options.A: Malnourished patients always refuse their oral medications
options.B: Hospital insurance policies automatically extend stays for underweight individuals
options.C: Their body lacks the nutritional fuel needed to fight infection and heal
options.D: Doctors cannot discharge anyone who has lost any body weight

explanation: You've got this! Healing requires energy and raw materials. Without them, recovery slows down and complications take longer to clear up.

question: What does the term 'bereavement' mean in nursing care?

options.A: The physical pain felt in the chest after a loss
options.B: The deliberate suppression of sad emotions
options.C: The objective state of having lost someone through death
options.D: The outward religious rituals performed at a funeral

explanation: You've got this! Bereavement is simply the factual reality that someone you care about has passed away. It is the starting point where grief and mourning begin.

question: As teenagers grow up, what is the biggest change that happens in their social lives?

options.A: Social interaction with others stops completely
options.B: Peer groups become the primary frame of reference
options.C: Family units become the sole source of social interaction
options.D: Work colleagues replace all school friendships

explanation: It's totally normal for teens to lean more on their friends and peer groups as they figure out who they are!

question: A patient keeps getting severe bacterial infections. Which lab values should the nurse check first to see how their antibody defenses are doing?

options.A: Serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen
options.B: Serum immunoglobulin levels (IgG, IgA, IgM)
options.C: Liver enzymes (ALT and AST)
options.D: Fasting serum cholesterol and lipids

explanation: Immunoglobulins (antibodies) handle our humoral immunity. Checking IgG, IgA, and IgM levels helps us see if an antibody shortage is leaving the patient wide open to infections.

question: Why is it important that junior health workers feel comfortable speaking up about safety concerns?

options.A: Every team member can spot errors and protect patient safety
options.B: It speeds up staff promotion processes in the clinic
options.C: It eliminates the need for any written medical records
options.D: It allows junior staff to take over the doctor's duties

explanation: Open communication across all ranks ensures that overlooked risks or mistakes are caught early by any attentive team member. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T12#GNS124_U5_T12_h7)

question: Why do healthcare facilities use incident reports?

options.A: To calculate the patient's final hospital expenses
options.B: To improve safety and prevent future occurrences
options.C: To provide permanent legal evidence inside patient charts
options.D: To find which specific nurse to blame for a mistake

explanation: That is right! Incident reports help hospitals catch system hazards so they can fix policies and protect future patients.

question: What is an immediate, frontline nursing action when a patient expresses normal pregnancy ambivalence?

options.A: Validating feelings and normalizing the experience
options.B: Immediately prescribing high-dose antidepressant medications
options.C: Reporting the patient to child protective services
options.D: Advising the patient to stop attending antenatal clinics

explanation: You've got it! Letting mums know their mixed emotions are totally normal brings instant relief and builds trust.

question: How do bedside nurses play a direct role in improving healthcare quality?

options.A: By conducting all hospital building maintenance and equipment repairs
options.B: By rewriting all state healthcare laws and national medical policies
options.C: By managing the financial investments and budget allocations of the hospital
options.D: By participating in safety committees and suggesting workflow redesigns

explanation: Spot on! Because nurses work hands-on with daily systems, their practical ideas are gold for creating safer workflows and better patient care.

question: What is usually the very first sign that makes a woman realize she needs to check her breast?

options.A: Severe, sharp pain throughout both breasts
options.B: Complete disappearance of the normal breast tissue
options.C: A hard, painless, and irregular breast lump
options.D: A sudden fever with generalized body weakness

explanation: A painless, hard lump is the classic red flag. Because it doesn't hurt at first, many women unfortunately ignore it.

question: How do oxygen and carbon dioxide move across the alveolar-capillary membrane?

options.A: Active transport
options.B: Simple diffusion
options.C: Pinocytosis
options.D: Osmotic pressure

explanation: Gases move naturally across the thin membrane from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration without using cellular energy. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h4)

question: What should you tell a patient about how much topical cream to use?

options.A: Apply a thick layer so it cures the condition faster
options.B: Use only the exact amount prescribed by the doctor
options.C: Stop using the cream as soon as symptoms disappear
options.D: Double the dose if the skin looks very dry or scaly

explanation: More isn't always better! Piling on extra cream won't speed up healing, but it can cause skin thinning and side effects.

question: Why is informed consent a crucial part of pre-test counselling?

options.A: It legally protects the hospital from paying for laboratory reagents
options.B: It forces the patient to buy their own testing kits from the pharmacy
options.C: It guarantees that testing is completely voluntary and understood by the client
options.D: It ensures the test results will automatically be published in local newspapers

explanation: Voluntary testing respects patient autonomy and builds trust between the client and the healthcare provider. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h2)

question: Why are patients with swollen bellies (ascites) told to cut down on salt?

options.A: Salt makes the body hold onto water, worsening fluid in the belly
options.B: Sodium directly destroys liver cells if eaten in large amounts
options.C: Sodium prevents the body from absorbing water pills (diuretics)
options.D: High salt diets instantly trigger severe esophageal bleeding

explanation: Remember the golden rule: water follows salt! Keeping sodium low stops the kidneys from holding onto extra water, easing belly swelling.

question: What are the three core functions of public health?

options.A: Inpatient care, pharmacy, and laboratory
options.B: Planning, budgeting, and marketing
options.C: Assessment, policy development, and assurance
options.D: Diagnosis, surgery, and rehabilitation

explanation: The recognized framework for public health activities consists of assessment, policy development, and assurance. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h5)

question: Which pancreatic hormone is primarily responsible for lowering blood glucose levels?

options.A: Cortisol
options.B: Thyroxine
options.C: Glucagon
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Insulin facilitates the movement of glucose out of the bloodstream and into body cells, effectively lowering circulating blood sugar levels. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T5#GNS211_U1_T5_h3)

question: Even though prolactin is high during pregnancy, why doesn't heavy milk production start right away?

options.A: Oxytocin suppresses milk synthesis until the baby is born
options.B: High levels of estrogen and progesterone block prolactin action
options.C: The alveoli are not yet fully formed until labor begins
options.D: The placenta actively destroys prolactin in the maternal blood

explanation: During pregnancy, the placenta keeps high levels of estrogen and progesterone around, which acts like a block on full milk production. Once the baby and placenta are delivered, that block lifts!

question: How do modified utensils with built-in grips help a patient with failing fine motor control?

options.A: They compensate for weak grip strength and hand tremors
options.B: They completely cure the underlying nerve degeneration
options.C: They prevent the patient from feeling hungry
options.D: They make the food taste better and digest faster

explanation: Specialized grips provide better purchase for weak hands, allowing the patient to continue feeding themselves without assistance. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h5)

question: What happens to most of the developing follicles in the ovary during a typical cycle?

options.A: They turn directly into the corpus luteum
options.B: They migrate into the fallopian tubes
options.C: They all release eggs simultaneously
options.D: They degenerate through atresia

explanation: Even though a group of follicles starts growing each month, only one becomes the champion (dominant) follicle. The rest quietly break down through a natural process called atresia.

question: What makes writing patient notes (charting) tricky for flight nurses during a journey?

options.A: A complete lack of paper and pens in the cabin
options.B: Constant aircraft motion and turbulence
options.C: Patients refusing to share their medical history
options.D: Strict laws forbidding written notes in aircraft

explanation: Right on! Trying to write neat, legible notes while the aircraft is shaking and bumping from turbulence is definitely a challenge.

question: Which of these is NOT a good strategy for helping a patient stick to a therapeutic diet long-term?

options.A: Involving family members in meal planning
options.B: Using herbs and spices to keep meals flavorful
options.C: Making gradual and sustainable food swaps
options.D: Making sudden, extreme food restrictions overnight without preparation

explanation: Going cold turkey on all your favorite foods overnight usually leads to burnout. Small, steady changes work best!

question: What happens right away if a food sample is collected poorly or transported in warm conditions?

options.A: The food sample automatically sterilizes itself
options.B: The laboratory test results become invalid
options.C: The sample gains extra vitamins and minerals
options.D: Pathogens instantly transform into harmless spores

explanation: That's correct! If food isn't kept cool during transport, bacteria will either multiply or die off, meaning the lab won't see the true picture of what was in the food.

question: Why do combined oral contraceptive pills carry a risk of blood clots?

options.A: Daily pill swallowing thickens the blood cells directly
options.B: Progestin causes severe dehydration in the body
options.C: Sugar pills trigger an inflammatory immune response
options.D: Estrogen stimulates clotting factors in the liver

explanation: Think of it this way: the estrogen part of the pill encourages the liver to produce more clotting proteins, which can raise the chance of blood clots in some patients.

question: What clothing rule is a must when you enter the restricted zone of an operating suite?

options.A: No special clothing or personal protective gear is needed
options.B: Street clothes and ordinary shoes are allowed without restriction
options.C: Full surgical attire including masks and hair covers is mandatory
options.D: Only lab coats worn over regular clothes are required

explanation: Correct! Since this zone gets closest to the sterile field, wearing complete scrubs, caps, and masks keeps everyone safe from accidental contamination.

question: What does the popular '60/60 rule' recommend when using earphones or headphones?

options.A: Listening at no more than sixty percent volume for sixty minutes daily
options.B: Taking a sixty-minute break after every sixty steps taken
options.C: Keeping the device sixty inches away from the ears at all times
options.D: Using headphones for no more than sixty hours a week

explanation: The 60/60 rule is an easy trick to protect your ears from loud music damage. Try keeping your volume at 60% or lower for no more than 60 minutes a day!

question: Where do we usually find the stubborn bacteria spores that cause tetanus?

options.A: Purified bottled water
options.B: Soil
options.C: Clean indoor air
options.D: Fresh pasteurized milk

explanation: Tetanus spores love hanging out in the dirt and soil, waiting for a little cut or scrape to sneak into the body.

question: A patient receiving neck radiation asks if they can use their favorite scented lotion on the area. What is the best reply?

options.A: Recommend using only approved, gentle, fragrance-free products to avoid further skin irritation
options.B: Suggest stopping all skin hygiene practices until the entire course of treatment finishes
options.C: Advise scrubbing the skin firmly with a washcloth before applying any cream or lotion
options.D: Encourage applying the scented lotion generously right before each radiation session

explanation: You're thinking like a caring nurse! Radiation makes skin very sensitive, so stick to mild, fragrance-free lotions approved by the care team.

question: What is a major nursing priority during the immediate postoperative period following a gynecological surgery?

options.A: Discontinuing all pain medication immediately
options.B: Removing surgical dressings within the first hour
options.C: Monitoring vital signs for signs of hemorrhage
options.D: Initiating rigorous high-intensity aerobic exercise

explanation: Vascular pelvic tissues carry a high risk of bleeding post-surgery, making vital sign monitoring critical to catch hemorrhage early. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T7#GNS311_U1_T7_h6)

question: A nurse uses a blood pressure cuff that is far too small for an adult patient with a large arm. What kind of reading is most likely to result?

options.A: A falsely low blood pressure reading
options.B: A reading showing zero systolic pressure
options.C: A falsely high blood pressure reading
options.D: A completely normal and accurate reading

explanation: Using a cuff that is too small requires excessive pressure to occlude the branch artery, leading to an artificially inflated blood pressure measurement. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T2#GNS313_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which of the following is a major risk factor for respiratory complications in the ICU?

options.A: Eating a high-protein hospital diet
options.B: Mechanical ventilation and artificial airways
options.C: Having normal blood pressure readings
options.D: Walking in the hallway twice a day

explanation: Artificial airways and mechanical ventilators bypass normal body defenses, making it much easier for bacteria to cause pneumonia and for lung tissue to collapse. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h2)

question: You check a new mother's uterus and find it feels soft and boggy instead of firm. What should you do first?

options.A: Encourage her to walk in the hallway
options.B: Apply an ice pack to the perineum
options.C: Gentle fundal massage to help it contract
options.D: Give her a routine oral laxative

explanation: A soft or 'boggy' uterus needs a gentle massage to firm up and stop heavy bleeding. You are keeping her safe!

question: What are the earliest vital sign clues that a patient might be bleeding internally after a biopsy?

options.A: Sudden high blood pressure and a very slow pulse
options.B: Falling blood pressure and a fast heart rate
options.C: Rising fever and flushed skin
options.D: Slow, deep breathing with high oxygen levels

explanation: Spot on! When blood is lost inside, blood volume drops. The heart beats faster to make up for it, while blood pressure starts to slide down.

question: A community health nurse in rural Nigeria uses a mobile phone app to track children's immunizations. What does this show?

options.A: The integration of technology into modern community health practice
options.B: A complete return to medieval religious care giving methods
options.C: The abandonment of primary healthcare principles
options.D: An illegal practice that violates public health policies

explanation: Just like you using this CBT app on your phone, modern nurses use digital tools every day to make healthcare smarter and faster!

question: Which environmental hazard should be removed from a room to protect a patient with a mobility impairment?

options.A: Heavy wooden wardrobes
options.B: Overhead ceiling lights
options.C: Loose throw rugs
options.D: Wall-mounted handrails

explanation: Loose rugs slip easily under feet or mobility devices, making them a leading cause of preventable indoor falls. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h8)

question: What is the best way to ask a patient about suspected abuse during a nursing assessment?

options.A: Using private, non-judgmental, and direct questions
options.B: Warning the patient about the legal consequences of lying
options.C: Waiting until the patient brings up the topic spontaneously
options.D: Asking in front of family members to get confirmation

explanation: You've got this! A private, gentle, and non-blaming approach makes patients feel safe enough to open up.

question: What is the main goal of ergonomics in the workplace?

options.A: Inspecting the concrete strength of the building
options.B: Setting exact employee salaries and bonuses
options.C: Fitting workstations and tools to match human body limits
options.D: Managing the menu in the staff cafeteria

explanation: Exactly! Ergonomics is all about designing work tools and chairs to fit the human body, preventing physical strain.

question: How do fontanelles help protect an infant's brain during early childhood?

options.A: By acting as shock absorbers and allowing room for the brain to expand
options.B: By keeping the inner ear bones aligned during early feeding
options.C: By sealing tightly to prevent blood from pooling under the scalp
options.D: By producing extra cerebrospinal fluid to nourish the growing brain

explanation: Exactly! They act like mini shock absorbers against bumps and give the rapidly growing brain all the space it needs.

question: A pregnant woman is worried about dark patches on her face and a line on her belly. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Reassure her that these are normal hormonal changes that usually fade after birth
options.B: Advise her to scrub the dark areas hard with soap every morning
options.C: Explain that these marks indicate a dangerous vitamin deficiency in her diet
options.D: Tell her to immediately see a dermatologist for emergency skin surgery

explanation: A warm, reassuring word goes a long way! Explaining that these marks are normal helps anxious mums relax.

question: What is a primary nursing responsibility regarding advance directives upon patient admission?

options.A: Deciding whether the living will is legally valid without a doctor
options.B: Writing the legal documents for the patient using hospital letterhead
options.C: Notifying the local court system that a new patient has arrived
options.D: Asking about existing directives and placing copies in the medical record

explanation: Nurses routinely screen for advance directives upon admission to ensure the care team knows the patient's preferences from the start. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h7)

question: What is a transect walk during an environmental scan?

options.A: A systematic walk through the community to observe conditions firsthand
options.B: A physical exercise routine taught to pregnant women at the clinic
options.C: A laboratory test used to measure water contamination levels
options.D: A legal court session held to resolve community land disputes

explanation: Correct! A transect walk means walking a set path through the community to see housing, sanitation, and hazards with your own eyes.

question: Why is it best to look for local strengths in the community before asking for outside donations?

options.A: External organizations refuse to work with community nurses
options.B: Local materials are always completely free of charge
options.C: Outside donors are legally banned from helping health clinics
options.D: It builds self-reliance so the program can keep running long-term

explanation: Spot on! Using local assets empowers the community so the project doesn't collapse the moment outside help stops.

question: When public health nurses talk about 'community structure', what are they mostly looking at?

options.A: The financial budget of the local government
options.B: How people are organized and how power is distributed
options.C: The physical blueprint of houses in a neighborhood
options.D: The exact number of hospital beds in a local clinic

explanation: Think of community structure as the backbone of the neighborhood: who holds influence, how groups connect, and how leadership works. Spotting this helps you know who to talk to when you want to start a health project!

question: A baby is born with spina bifida, where the spinal column is open in the lower back. Which early process did not close properly?

options.A: Formation of the endoderm layer
options.B: Implantation of the blastocyst
options.C: Division of cells during early cleavage
options.D: Neural tube closure during neurulation

explanation: That's right. Spina bifida happens when the neural tube doesn't fully seal up during the early weeks of pregnancy. This is why folic acid is so vital!

question: An elderly patient with unsteady balance is admitted to your ward. What is your best first nursing action?

options.A: Tie the patient securely to the bed to prevent movement
options.B: Ensure the call bell is within reach and pathways are clear
options.C: Restrict all out-of-bed activity for the entire hospital stay
options.D: Turn off the room lights at night so the patient sleeps

explanation: Brilliant! Keeping pathways free of clutter and making sure they can easily call for help keeps them safe without using harsh restraints.

question: Which sign is a major red flag for a developing perineal hematoma after delivery?

options.A: Severe, sharp pelvic pain out of proportion to the wound
options.B: Sudden high fever accompanied by shaking chills
options.C: Complete absence of lochia discharge for several days
options.D: Inability to feel the urge to urinate or empty the bladder

explanation: A hematoma is a hidden pool of blood building up under the tissues. It creates intense, throbbing pressure that feels way worse than a normal sore stitch.

question: What is the main goal of primary prevention in neurological nursing?

options.A: To rehabilitate a patient after a massive stroke
options.B: To cure advanced stages of Alzheimer's disease
options.C: To stop a neurological disease before it starts
options.D: To detect brain tumors through early screening tests

explanation: Think of primary prevention as your shield. It focuses entirely on health promotion and stopping conditions from developing in the first place.

question: A nurse leads a support group to help patients with chronic bipolar disorder prevent relapse. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Primary prevention
options.B: Universal prevention
options.C: Secondary prevention
options.D: Tertiary prevention

explanation: Tertiary prevention involves managing established, chronic conditions to reduce disability and prevent worsening or relapse. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h2)

question: What is the main meaning of 'food insecurity'?

options.A: Temporary fasting practiced during religious or cultural holiday seasons
options.B: A personal choice to go on a strict weight-loss diet for health reasons
options.C: Lack of consistent access to enough safe and nutritious food for a healthy life
options.D: Having too many grocery stores in a single neighborhood community

explanation: Food insecurity means a person or family never quite knows where their next wholesome meal is coming from.

question: Why are women biologically more at risk of getting STIs than men?

options.A: The rapid turnover rate of vaginal epithelial cells
options.B: The large area of delicate mucosal tissue in the female reproductive tract
options.C: Lower natural antibody counts in female sweat
options.D: A higher resting internal body temperature in the pelvis

explanation: The fragile lining inside the female reproductive tract easily forms tiny micro-tears during sex, giving germs an easy way to enter the body.

question: Who is at the highest risk of catching Lassa fever in a hospital?

options.A: A nurse caring for a bleeding patient without proper personal protective equipment
options.B: A pharmacist dispensing oral medications from a secure dispensary
options.C: A patient admitted to the medical ward for severe malaria
options.D: A visitor sitting quietly across the room from a stable patient

explanation: Direct contact with infectious body fluids like blood without barrier protection puts healthcare workers at serious risk.

question: When does an event situation officially become a mass casualty incident (MCI)?

options.A: The number of injured people exceeds available medical resources.
options.B: More than ten people faint from the outdoor heat.
options.C: All electricity to the venue suddenly fails.
options.D: The police decide to shut down the event early.

explanation: An MCI isn't just about a specific number of people—it's when there are simply more injured folks than the medical staff and supplies can handle at once.

question: Which crucial supplement do nurses always advise early pregnant mothers to take to prevent spinal and brain birth defects?

options.A: Folic acid
options.B: Vitamin C
options.C: Calcium carbonate
options.D: Iron sulfate

explanation: Folic acid is a superstar vitamin for early pregnancy! It protects the baby's developing neural tube from serious defects.

question: What structural feature inside lymphatic vessels prevents the backward flow of lymph?

options.A: Valves
options.B: Nodes
options.C: Sphincters
options.D: Cilia

explanation: Lymphatic vessels contain one-way valves that ensure fluid moves only toward the heart. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h2)

question: How do adults usually approach learning differently from children?

options.A: Adults memorize facts faster without needing to understand the reason
options.B: Adults have no prior knowledge to connect new concepts to
options.C: Adults rely heavily on their prior life experiences and practical needs
options.D: Adults prefer complete dependence on the teacher for daily direction

explanation: Adults love to connect new lessons to what they've already lived through and want to know how the info helps them right now.

question: What is a common clinical pitfall when dealing with a patient showing signs of maladaptation?

options.A: Encouraging them to express their hidden fears and worries
options.B: Providing too much detailed education about their medication
options.C: Labeling the patient as difficult instead of recognizing psychological exhaustion
options.D: Checking their vital signs too frequently throughout the day

explanation: Viewing uncooperative behavior as a character flaw rather than a coping failure prevents nurses from offering the proper psychological support. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T6#GNS123_U1_T6_h5)

question: Which of the following is a clear indication for starting dialysis in acute renal failure?

options.A: Normal laboratory values for serum creatinine and blood urea
options.B: A mild and stable increase in the patient's daily appetite
options.C: A temporary decrease in blood pressure caused by mild dehydration
options.D: Severe and persistent hyperkalemia that resists medical treatment

explanation: Dangerous electrolyte imbalances like unmanageable high potassium are a primary reason to start urgent dialysis. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T6#GNS213_U4_T6_h7)

question: How can the profit-driven nature of private food companies negatively impact public health?

options.A: It prevents supermarkets from ever selling fresh fruits and vegetables.
options.B: It requires the government to take full ownership of local grocery stores.
options.C: It can lead to the overproduction and marketing of cheap, ultra-processed foods.
options.D: It forces all farmers to stop growing staple grains like rice and maize.

explanation: Profit motives often encourage companies to produce inexpensive, highly processed foods that contribute to rising rates of obesity and chronic illnesses. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T029#GNS227_U2_T029_h5)

question: What do we call a loss that can be clearly seen and verified by everyone around, like losing a limb or a loved one?

options.A: A loss that is only felt internally by the affected individual
options.B: A loss of money or property caused by economic changes
options.C: A loss that occurs only during old age and natural retirement
options.D: A loss that can be recognized and verified by other people

explanation: Spot on! An actual loss is tangible. It's something both the patient and outsiders can clearly see, touch, or acknowledge, like an amputation or death.

question: Why is a small markup added to the cost price of DRF drugs?

options.A: To punish patients who buy drugs late in the evening
options.B: To make the hospital pharmacy richer than private stores
options.C: To pay bonuses to nurses on night shift duty
options.D: To cover minor operational costs and protect against inflation

explanation: That tiny extra amount isn't for profit—it helps cover transport costs and keeps the fund strong against rising prices.

question: What is the main goal of respecting patient autonomy in end-of-life care?

options.A: Reducing the workload of the attending nursing staff
options.B: Ensuring family members make all major medical decisions
options.C: Allowing the patient to keep control over their choices
options.D: Speeding up the discharge process from the facility

explanation: Respecting autonomy means empowering the patient to direct their own care and make meaningful decisions about their remaining time. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h2)

question: Which health intervention is a community volunteer most likely to assist with during a school health week?

options.A: Administering mass deworming tablets and educating on hygiene
options.B: Performing complex orthopedic surgeries in the school library
options.C: Conducting annual performance appraisals for teaching staff
options.D: Auditing the financial accounts of the school cafeteria

explanation: Community volunteers frequently assist with public health campaigns like mass deworming, vaccination, and basic hygiene promotion. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h4)

question: Which of these is a classic sign of a torn urethra in a male patient?

options.A: Painless swelling of the scrotum
options.B: Sudden uncontrollable diarrhea
options.C: Blood at the urethral meatus
options.D: Yellowing of the eye sclera

explanation: Seeing a bit of blood right at the opening of the penis tells us immediately that the urethra might be torn. Great clinical clue to keep in mind!

question: Which of these options has NO effect on how well your body absorbs nutrients?

options.A: The health and integrity of the villi
options.B: The pH of the digestive tract
options.C: Intestinal motility speed
options.D: The astrological sign of the patient

explanation: Haha, definitely not your horoscope! Nutrient absorption depends strictly on physical and chemical factors like gut movement, pH, and mucosal health.

question: Why do nursing students need to learn about different sources of knowledge?

options.A: To eliminate the need for clinical experience entirely
options.B: To memorize every historical medical text ever written
options.C: To understand why clinical guidelines change and why evidence matters
options.D: To learn how to diagnose patients without a doctor

explanation: Knowing where knowledge comes from helps you see why nursing care changes for the better as new evidence comes to light. You've got this!

question: Why is planning so important on a hospital ward before daily tasks begin?

options.A: It allows nurses to avoid direct patient care responsibilities.
options.B: It prevents chaos and ensures everyone works toward the same goals.
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for emergency staff meetings.
options.D: It guarantees that the hospital will never run out of money.

explanation: A solid plan gives your team a clear roadmap so everyone coordinates their efforts smoothly instead of guessing what to do next!

question: When does tertiary prevention happen along the care continuum?

options.A: After a diagnosis and treatment have already occurred
options.B: While administering vaccines in a community health clinic
options.C: During routine screening tests for healthy people
options.D: Before any exposure to environmental toxins happens

explanation: Tertiary prevention steps in after treatment to help patients recover, manage long-term effects, and get back to daily life.

question: What is the Hawthorne effect when observing staff nurses during audits?

options.A: A sudden spike in patient admissions during the rainy seasonal period
options.B: The mathematical formula used to calculate hospital bed occupancy rates
options.C: The rapid physical exhaustion nurses feel toward the end of a night shift
options.D: Staff changing their behavior temporarily because they know they are being watched

explanation: The Hawthorne effect reminds us that people naturally change how they work when they know someone is watching them closely.

question: Which lab finding under a microscope points strongly to a kidney infection (pyelonephritis) rather than a simple bladder infection?

options.A: Calcium oxalate crystals
options.B: Squamous epithelial cells
options.C: White blood cell casts
options.D: Isolated red blood cells

explanation: Casts are tiny mold-shaped clumps that form way up inside the kidney tubes. Finding white cell casts tells us the infection has traveled high up into the kidneys!

question: A patient with Korsakoff syndrome insists on going home to feed a pet dog that died years ago. How should you respond?

options.A: Agree that the dog is waiting at home for them
options.B: Gently redirect the patient to a current activity without arguing
options.C: Ignore the patient and leave the room immediately
options.D: Argue firmly until the patient admits the dog is dead

explanation: Arguing will only upset or confuse them. The kindest nursing move is to stay calm, validate their feelings softly, and smoothly guide them to a new activity.

question: A patient is given a drug that blocks parasympathetic activity. Which symptom would you most likely see?

options.A: Rapid digestion and frequent urination
options.B: Slowed heart rate and excessive drooling
options.C: Dry mouth and decreased bowel sounds
options.D: Constricted pupils and low blood pressure

explanation: The parasympathetic system is your 'rest-and-digest' mode. Blocking it stops secretions and slows the gut down, resulting in a dry mouth and sluggish digestion.

question: Which classroom setup helps prevent you from feeling sleepy during long lectures?

options.A: Bright neon paint and loud music
options.B: Proper lighting and good ventilation
options.C: Complete darkness with shut windows
options.D: Tight, cramped seating to save space

explanation: Fresh air and good lighting keep headaches and sleepiness away, helping you stay sharp and focused while your lecturer is talking.

question: What is the main purpose of advance care planning?

options.A: To ensure patient wishes guide future treatment
options.B: To let healthcare providers make all choices
options.C: To speed up the legal probate process
options.D: To reduce hospital cleaning costs

explanation: Spot on! Advance care planning makes sure the patient's voice is heard and respected, even if they can no longer speak for themselves later on.

question: Why should a research report use clear and simple language?

options.A: Busy healthcare workers must easily understand and apply the findings
options.B: Journals will reject any paper that uses simple everyday language
options.C: Patients require the full report to manage their own treatments
options.D: Medical terminology is banned in modern academic publishing

explanation: Wards are busy places! Clear writing helps nurses quickly grab key facts and use them at the bedside.

question: Which of these is a major red flag that supervisors look out for during a data audit?

options.A: Reporting zero waste while consumption numbers are very high
options.B: Having more than two nurses sign the document
options.C: Submitting the monthly report on the exact final day
options.D: Using blue ink instead of black ink on the monitoring form

explanation: Spot on! In a busy clinic, zero waste is almost impossible. It usually means the numbers were guessed or made up.

question: Why is it important for a nurse to explain each step before starting a reproductive assessment?

options.A: To distract the patient from physical pain
options.B: To decrease patient anxiety and build trust
options.C: To speed up the total time spent in the room
options.D: To fulfill strict legal billing requirements

explanation: Spot on! Reproductive exams can feel intimidating. Explaining what you are about to do calms nerves and helps the patient trust you.

question: What makes an auto-disable (AD) syringe special?

options.A: It locks or breaks after a single use to prevent reuse
options.B: It changes color when exposed to direct sunlight
options.C: It can be sterilized in boiling water up to ten times
options.D: It has a detachable needle that can be safely recapped

explanation: Correct! AD syringes jam or break right after the first injection so nobody can accidentally reuse them on another patient.

question: When do program evaluations usually take place during a health project's lifecycle?

options.A: Every single morning during the nurse handover briefing
options.B: At specific milestones, such as midterm and project completion
options.C: Randomly without any set schedule or plan
options.D: Only after funding has completely run out and staff have left

explanation: Evaluations are scheduled check-ins at key points (like midway or at the end) to see how well the project is doing.

question: Why do we apply a cold pack to an insect sting right after it happens?

options.A: It numbs the skin permanently to prevent any future scarring
options.B: It constricts blood vessels to slow venom absorption and reduce swelling
options.C: It opens up local capillaries to flush out the venom faster
options.D: It completely neutralizes the chemical composition of the insect toxin

explanation: Cold makes the local blood vessels narrow down (vasoconstriction), slowing down how fast the venom spreads while keeping pain and swelling low.

question: Which of these is NOT a common sign of meningitis?

options.A: High fever and body chills
options.B: Sudden complete paralysis of the lower limbs
options.C: Severe and pounding headache
options.D: Stiff and painful neck movement

explanation: Spot on! Meningitis causes terrible headaches, fever, and a stiff neck, but leg paralysis is not a standard sign of the infection.

question: Which patient position is most commonly used for a routine proctoscopy?

options.A: Left lateral Sims' position
options.B: Prone flat on the abdomen
options.C: Trendelenburg flat position
options.D: Supine with legs in stirrups

explanation: You got it! The left lateral (or Sims') position is the standard, most comfortable posture for a patient during this exam.

question: Why do community nurses need to collaborate with other professionals when solving health problems?

options.A: It reduces the cost of running primary healthcare clinics
options.B: It ensures that doctors make all decisions without community input
options.C: Complex health problems require diverse skills and coordinated efforts
options.D: It eliminates the need for nurses to conduct home visits

explanation: Spot on! Because health is tied to housing, water, and social life, different professionals have to team up to find real solutions.

question: What is the main financial goal of Community-Based Rehabilitation (CBR) programs?

options.A: Providing multi-million-dollar corporate loans
options.B: Empowering individuals through local skill acquisition and vocational training
options.C: Ending the need for all medical care
options.D: Taking over family legal responsibilities

explanation: CBR helps people learn practical trades using local resources so they can stand on their own feet financially.

question: If a patient has a blockage in their intestinal lymph vessels (lacteals), which nutrient will be hardest to absorb?

options.A: Proteins
options.B: Carbohydrates
options.C: Water
options.D: Fats

explanation: Spot on! Since dietary fats rely on the lymphatic system for transport, a blockage there means fat absorption takes a major hit.

question: Why are functional emergency referral systems so important for pregnant women in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: Government policy requires all babies to be born in teaching hospitals
options.B: Patients prefer to pay higher fees at tertiary hospitals rather than local clinics
options.C: Primary health clinics cannot manage severe obstetric emergencies like ruptured uterus or eclampsia
options.D: Primary health centers do not keep any medical records of pregnant women

explanation: Local clinics are great for routine antenatal care, but if a life-threatening emergency like severe eclampsia happens, patients need quick transport to a bigger hospital with a doctor and blood bank.

question: Where should the toxic ash from burning medical waste be dumped?

options.A: Shallow trenches dug right behind the hospital
options.B: Open community rubbish pits near local farms
options.C: Secure engineered landfills with protective liners
options.D: Standard municipal recycling bins for plastic

explanation: Incinerator ash has chemicals and toxins in it, so it must go into a specially lined landfill to protect our soil and drinking water.

question: A patient says they cannot afford the expensive imported supplements prescribed elsewhere. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Report the patient to the hospital management
options.B: Tell the patient to stop eating altogether
options.C: Tell them to borrow money to buy the brand
options.D: Help the patient find affordable local whole-food alternatives

explanation: Brilliant! As a nurse, you bridge the gap by showing patients how to get great nutrition using what is easily available around them.

question: A patient taking high-dose prednisone for six months reports feeling very hungry all the time and notices weight gain around the face and neck. What causes this?

options.A: Fluid is building up inside the brain tissue.
options.B: Steroids alter how the body stores fat and stimulates appetite.
options.C: The medication is destroying the thyroid gland completely.
options.D: The patient is secretly eating too much junk food at night.

explanation: Corticosteroids alter carbohydrate and fat metabolism, frequently causing increased appetite and fat redistribution. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h5)

question: What is another common medical name for cervical erosion?

options.A: Cervical carcinoma
options.B: Cervical ectropion
options.C: Cervical dysplasia
options.D: Cervical stenosis

explanation: You will often hear cervical erosion called cervical ectropion in the clinic. It just means the inner cells of the cervix have moved outward a bit. You've got this!

question: What is the primary purpose of performing a straight leg raise test on a patient complaining of back pain?

options.A: To grade the strength of the quadriceps muscle
options.B: To check for spinal nerve root irritation like sciatica
options.C: To measure the exact range of motion of the hip joint
options.D: To test for a torn meniscus inside the knee joint

explanation: Raising the straight leg stretches the sciatic nerve, reproducing radiating pain if a nerve root is compressed or inflamed. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T3#GNS222_U1_T3_h8)

question: What is a major goal of food fortification programs in Nigeria (like adding vitamins to oil and flour)?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of hospital buildings
options.B: To replace all local staple crops with imported grains
options.C: To increase the commercial shelf life of fresh meat
options.D: To combat widespread micronutrient deficiencies

explanation: Fortifying everyday foods helps protect whole communities from missing out on key vitamins and minerals.

question: Which physical sign do patients very often report when they are feeling extremely anxious?

options.A: Rapid heartbeat or palpitations
options.B: Sustained lowering of blood pressure
options.C: Uncontrolled weight gain over days
options.D: Permanent loss of skin pigmentation

explanation: Correct! When anxiety hits, adrenaline surges through the body, frequently causing a racing heart or palpitations.

question: What does the Drug Control Act primarily regulate?

options.A: The cleaning schedules of hospital wards
options.B: The daily salaries of nursing personnel
options.C: The handling and distribution of controlled substances
options.D: The construction of public healthcare clinics

explanation: The act focuses on controlling how dangerous drugs are moved, made, and supplied in the country. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h2)

question: What happens in a healthcare facility that loves to punish and blame staff?

options.A: Nurses become more eager to report system failures
options.B: Medical errors are completely eliminated from the wards
options.C: Interprofessional communication improves significantly
options.D: Staff hide their mistakes and near-misses out of fear

explanation: Spot on! A heavy blame culture drives mistakes underground. When staff are terrified of punishment, nobody speaks up so the team can learn from it.

question: What is the main goal of an emergency nursing assessment?

options.A: To establish a comprehensive family medical history
options.B: To diagnose the underlying chronic disease
options.C: To identify and manage life-threatening conditions immediately
options.D: To complete administrative insurance paperwork

explanation: When a patient comes in rushed and critical, your very first duty as a nurse is to find and fix immediate threats to life before anything else. You've got this!

question: Why is collecting health data but never analyzing or using it considered a bad practice?

options.A: It automatically invalidates all future requests for international donor grants
options.B: It violates international copyright laws regarding health registers
options.C: It wastes valuable time and resources while failing to improve community health outcomes
options.D: It causes immediate supply chain shortages in urban pharmacies

explanation: Collecting data takes hard work from nurses and patients. If no one looks at it to make decisions, that effort goes to waste!

question: How do Chi-Square hypotheses usually handle direction?

options.A: They are typically non-directional and test for any association
options.B: They must always predict a positive linear direction
options.C: They only evaluate single continuous variables
options.D: They measure the exact numerical difference between means

explanation: Keep it up! Standard Chi-Square tests simply ask if a connection exists overall, without needing to guess whether it goes up or down.

question: Why do we encourage new mothers to get up and walk around (ambulate) early after childbirth?

options.A: To speed up the immediate closure of the cervix
options.B: To reduce the risk of blood clots and improve circulation
options.C: To encourage the baby to sleep through the night
options.D: To prevent the mother from producing too much colostrum

explanation: Getting moving gets the blood pumping! It keeps circulation strong and stops blood from pooling in the legs, preventing dangerous clots. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h7)

question: Which hormone tells your kidneys to hold onto water by opening special channels in the collecting ducts?

options.A: Antidiuretic hormone
options.B: Thyroid-stimulating hormone
options.C: Atrial natriuretic peptide
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Spot on! ADH (Antidiuretic Hormone) steps in when you are low on fluids to make sure you don't pee away your precious water.

question: What is a major physical benefit of early ambulation on the respiratory system?

options.A: It prevents chronic asthma attacks from developing in adults
options.B: It completely stops the production of mucus in the airways
options.C: It allows the lungs to expand fully to prevent pneumonia
options.D: It lowers the total volume of oxygen required by the body

explanation: Being upright helps the lungs open up completely, which stops fluid and secretions from pooling and causing infections like pneumonia. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T3#GNS324_U6_T3_h1)

question: What tends to happen to the basal metabolic rate during long periods of severe calorie restriction?

options.A: It fluctuates every single hour
options.B: It slows down to conserve energy
options.C: It stops functioning completely
options.D: It increases to burn extra glucose

explanation: Correct! Your body is smart—when it senses very low food intake, it slows down its metabolism to save energy, which can make further weight loss slower.

question: What is the main lab test used to find parasite eggs in clinic patients?

options.A: Taking an X-ray of the chest cavity
options.B: Microscopic stool examination
options.C: Performing a standard throat swab culture
options.D: Measuring routine fasting blood glucose

explanation: Lab techs look at prepared stool samples under a microscope to spot the unique shapes of parasite eggs. Perfect!

question: A nurse wants to teach malaria prevention in a rural village with low literacy. What is the best design choice?

options.A: Include complex medical tables showing blood parasite counts over time.
options.B: Publish the guidelines exclusively in standard official government English.
options.C: Use clear local dialect translations paired with dominant, self-explanatory pictures.
options.D: Write long paragraphs explaining the exact life cycle of the female Anopheles mosquito.

explanation: Pictures combined with simple local language are a nurse's best friend for breaking through literacy and language barriers!

question: After a very tough loss on the children's ward, what best helps the nursing team cope with the stress?

options.A: Forcing the team to take on extra admissions to stay busy
options.B: Pretending the event did not happen to maintain normal routines
options.C: Punishing the nurses immediately for failing to save the patient
options.D: Providing a safe space for structured team debriefing and counseling

explanation: Talking through grief together in a supportive session helps nurses heal and prevents long-term emotional burnout.

question: What term describes the first menstrual period in adolescent females?

options.A: Menarche
options.B: Menopause
options.C: Thelarche
options.D: Ovulation

explanation: Menarche is the medical term for a young woman's very first menstrual bleeding, marking a key milestone in female physical maturation. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T19#GNS312_U3_T19_h2)

question: What signs tell you that a patient is taking too much levothyroxine?

options.A: Dry skin, lethargy, and facial swelling
options.B: Palpitations, nervousness, and weight loss
options.C: Slow resting heart rate and severe constipation
options.D: Extreme fatigue, weight gain, and cold intolerance

explanation: Too much hormone pushes the body into overdrive. It's like flipping from hypothyroidism straight into hyperthyroidism symptoms!

question: What is the primary purpose of health care financing?

options.A: Eliminating all private pharmacies in the country
options.B: Reducing the number of working nurses in public hospitals
options.C: Generating profits for international pharmaceutical companies
options.D: Raising, pooling, and allocating financial resources for health needs

explanation: Financing ensures that money is collected, grouped, and spent effectively to keep the health system running. [learn more](GST322_U4_T2#GST322_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why do middlemen often add to the final retail cost of food items?

options.A: The government requires a special tax for every person who touches food
options.B: Farmers pay brokers a fine for picking crops too early
options.C: Each handler adds a markup to cover their services and risks
options.D: Middlemen store food in expensive international warehouses

explanation: Every intermediary along the chain charges for their labor, transport, and potential losses, raising the cumulative price. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h5)

question: Why do healthcare planners conduct a community needs assessment before setting up PAC services?

options.A: To recruit international doctors for specialized surgeries
options.B: To penalize traditional healers practicing in the village
options.C: To understand local barriers, health data, and access challenges
options.D: To determine the exact cost of medical equipment imports

explanation: A needs assessment helps us see what real-life factors delay care in the community—like transport issues or cultural fears—so we can design services that truly help people.

question: How can you help a patient who complains that their low-sodium food tastes too bland?

options.A: Allow the patient to use regular table salt if they eat half the meal
options.B: Remove the food tray and wait until the next scheduled mealtime
options.C: Suggest using herbs, citrus, and salt-free spice blends for flavor
options.D: Tell the patient that bland food is a mandatory part of healing

explanation: Wonderful! Herbs, garlic, and lemon juice add fantastic flavor without any harmful sodium, making healthy eating much easier.

question: What is a key action public health nurses take to improve community nutrition?

options.A: Growing all the crops needed for the entire country inside hospitals
options.B: Organizing nutritional screenings and educating families on budget-friendly local meals
options.C: Passing strict laws to ban all processed foods globally
options.D: Taking over the management of international cargo shipping lines

explanation: Spot on! Nurses play a huge role by checking nutritional status and teaching families how to cook healthy, pocket-friendly local meals.

question: How many months in a row without a period does a woman need to confirm she has reached menopause?

options.A: Six consecutive months
options.B: Twenty-four consecutive months
options.C: Twelve consecutive months
options.D: Three consecutive months

explanation: To be sure the monthly cycle has stopped for good, doctors look for a full year (12 months) of no menstruation. You've got this!

question: Why do babies with chlamydial eye infections usually need treatment that goes through the whole body (systemic), not just eye drops?

options.A: Eye drops are too painful for a newborn to tolerate
options.B: Oral medications work faster than eye drops
options.C: Topical eye drops alone cannot clear the systemic infection
options.D: Systemic drugs prevent the development of fever

explanation: You nailed it! Chlamydia doesn't just hang out in the eye; it can hide in other areas like the throat, meaning oral or systemic meds are needed to fully kick it.

question: What is the earliest physical sign of puberty in boys?

options.A: A sudden linear height spurt
options.B: Growth of facial hair
options.C: Deepening of the voice
options.D: Enlargement of the testes

explanation: Spot on! Testicular growth is the very first clinical sign that male puberty has begun.

question: Which airway maneuver is safest to use when a neck injury is suspected?

options.A: Neck-hyperextension method
options.B: Rapid lateral neck rotation
options.C: Jaw-thrust maneuver
options.D: Head-tilt/chin-lift maneuver

explanation: The jaw-thrust maneuver opens the airway without moving or bending the cervical spine, protecting the patient from further spinal cord damage. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h3)

question: What is a primary role of a public health nurse in the community?

options.A: Connecting families to local health and social support resources
options.B: Writing national health policies for pharmaceutical companies
options.C: Managing the financial budgets of local government hospitals
options.D: Performing complex major surgeries in community centers

explanation: Public health nurses link individuals and families to clinics, support groups, and welfare services that promote wellbeing. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h7)

question: Who can show leadership in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Only the appointed director of nursing
options.B: Only nurses with over twenty years of experience
options.C: Any nurse guiding care and supervising colleagues
options.D: Hospital chief executive officers exclusively

explanation: You don't need a fancy title to be a leader! Leadership is about your actions and positive influence. Even as a junior or staff nurse, you lead every time you guide patient care or help a colleague.

question: Why is equitable distribution of funds across urban and rural clinics important?

options.A: To prevent rural health collapse and ensure all citizens have access to basic care
options.B: To make sure city hospitals get all the newest vehicles
options.C: To reduce the number of nurses working in rural areas
options.D: To satisfy international organizations without helping patients

explanation: Fair funding stops the concentration of resources only in cities while villages suffer without medicines. [learn more](GST322_U4_T2#GST322_U4_T2_h3)

question: A widow visits the clinic two years after her husband passed away, unable to return to work, sleep, or stop crying daily. What condition is she most likely experiencing?

options.A: Complicated grief
options.B: Acute depression
options.C: Normal mourning
options.D: Anticipatory grief

explanation: When intense grief symptoms persist for a very long time and severely disrupt daily life, it is classified as complicated grief. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h3)

question: Why is transparency critical when mobilising a community for health action?

options.A: It stops villagers from asking questions about disease names
options.B: It guarantees that the federal government will send more funds
options.C: It builds lasting trust between the health team and the public
options.D: It prevents nurses from working long hours at the clinic

explanation: Open communication about goals, resources, and challenges removes suspicion and encourages people to cooperate fully. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h2)

question: What term describes two different observers getting similar results when watching the same event?

options.A: The Hawthorne effect
options.B: Participant bias
options.C: Inter-rater reliability
options.D: Structured validity

explanation: Well done! 'Inter-rater reliability' simply means different observers agree and are consistent in how they score what they see.

question: How does visiting a patient in their own home change things compared to treating them in a hospital ward?

options.A: It places the nurse as a guest in the patient's personal space
options.B: It completely removes the need for professional boundaries
options.C: It stops patients from making decisions about their care
options.D: It gives the nurse total legal control over the household

explanation: Exactly! When you step into someone's home, you are stepping into their private domain as a guest. Remembering this helps you respect their space while providing great care.

question: What is the main purpose of tilting the X-ray table into different angles during a barium swallow?

options.A: To drain excess stomach fluids before the contrast is given
options.B: To help gravity coat the entire lining of the esophagus and stomach with barium
options.C: To prevent the patient from falling asleep during the procedure
options.D: To speed up the digestion of the barium into the bloodstream

explanation: Changing table positions ensures that the liquid barium flows over all mucosal surfaces so small defects or ulcers are not missed. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h4)

question: Why is a sputum culture ordered when a client has a persistent productive cough?

options.A: To identify the specific microorganism causing an infection
options.B: To measure the total daily volume of mucus production
options.C: To check if the client has smoked cigarettes recently
options.D: To evaluate how well the lungs exchange gases

explanation: Culturing mucus allows the laboratory to grow the infectious agent and determine which antibiotic will treat it best. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T2#GNS213_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why can't we use standard adult BMI cutoffs to assess health risks in children and teenagers?

options.A: Children's bones are softer, which skews the standard imperial calculation method
options.B: Growing bodies experience natural shifts in body fat and height that change with age and sex
options.C: Pediatric scales cannot measure weight with the precision needed for a standard BMI
options.D: Children do not have enough muscle mass to make the mathematical formula work

explanation: Spot on! Kids and teens grow fast, so their body fat and height change constantly relative to their age and sex. That's why we use special growth charts instead!

question: How do micronutrients differ from macronutrients?

options.A: Micronutrients provide twice as many calories per gram as macronutrients
options.B: Micronutrients are only necessary during times of severe physical illness
options.C: Micronutrients are needed in much smaller amounts and do not directly provide energy
options.D: Micronutrients are manufactured inside the human liver rather than eaten

explanation: Vitamins and minerals (micronutrients) are like tiny sparks that help body processes run smoothly, even though they don't give direct fuel like carbs do.

question: A community health nurse is talking to abattoir (slaughterhouse) workers about their daily risks. Which animal-borne diseases should be the main focus?

options.A: Cerebrospinal meningitis
options.B: Cholera and typhoid fever
options.C: Anthrax and brucellosis
options.D: Malaria and yellow fever

explanation: You nailed it! Because abattoir workers handle livestock directly, they are at higher risk for zoonotic infections like anthrax and brucellosis.

question: What is the best tool to use for smoothing out rough nail edges after clipping?

options.A: A sharp surgical scissor
options.B: A metal cuticle pusher
options.C: A stiff plastic brush
options.D: An emery board or nail file

explanation: Correct! A nail file or emery board gently buffs away sharp, jagged edges without splitting the nail plate.

question: What is an effective way to help a hypertensive patient reduce their sodium intake?

options.A: Telling them to completely stop eating all forms of food
options.B: Advise them to rely entirely on restaurant meals
options.C: Suggesting they double their daily intake of canned foods
options.D: Teaching them how to read food labels and use herbs instead of salt

explanation: Practical education gives patients actionable tools like label reading and alternative flavorings to manage their health successfully. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h7)

question: What is a major advantage of cross-sectional research?

options.A: It requires zero participation from human subjects
options.B: It is relatively quick and cost-effective to conduct
options.C: It proves the exact cause of chronic diseases over time
options.D: It eliminates all forms of human bias automatically

explanation: No need to wait years! Cross-sectional studies save precious time and money because everything happens in one go.

question: What is the correct nursing action when a mentally competent adult client refuses a prescribed blood transfusion?

options.A: Respect the refusal, educate the client on the risks, and notify the attending doctor
options.B: Threaten to discharge the client immediately from the hospital ward
options.C: Call security officers to hold the client down during the procedure
options.D: Administer the blood transfusion secretly while the client is sleeping

explanation: Competent adults have the right to refuse treatment, and nurses must document this while informing the medical team. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h4)

question: Why is it important to check in on a teen's mental health during reproductive health visits?

options.A: Hospital insurance requires a psychological evaluation for pills
options.B: Psychiatric drugs can cure all sexually transmitted infections
options.C: Mental health struggles and reproductive health are closely linked
options.D: Anxiety directly stops the physical growth of bones

explanation: You nailed it! Emotional well-being deeply affects the choices teens make about relationships, safety, and their bodies. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h6)

question: Which of the following is a classic example of a polygenic human trait?

options.A: Tongue rolling
options.B: Blood type ABO
options.C: Height
options.D: Huntington disease

explanation: Height is controlled by many different genes interacting together, making it a polygenic trait. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h4)

question: A nurse finishes emptying a utility bin filled with used dressings and removes her heavy utility gloves. What is the immediate next step she should take?

options.A: Drink clean water to prevent dehydration
options.B: Perform hand hygiene with soap and water or alcohol rub
options.C: Write an incident report in the ward register
options.D: Put on a fresh pair of sterile surgical gloves

explanation: Hand hygiene is always mandatory immediately after taking off gloves, as microscopic tears in gloves can let germs reach the skin. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h8)

question: What is maceration in the context of skin care?

options.A: Skin becoming completely numb to all touch
options.B: Skin turning completely black from cold temperatures
options.C: Skin growing extra thick layers like a hard shell
options.D: Skin becoming soft and broken down from too much moisture

explanation: Maceration happens when moisture stays on the skin too long, making the tissue weak and prone to damage. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h8)

question: Why are vital statistics like death registries important for health surveillance?

options.A: They measure the trading volume of the local agricultural market.
options.B: They calculate the daily water supply pressure in the city.
options.C: They help track causes of death and overall population health trends.
options.D: They show which political party won the local government election.

explanation: Death registries give us a big-picture view of what is really killing people in our communities, guiding where public health help is needed most.

question: What is the very first thing you should do if you realize a medication error has happened?

options.A: Write an angry message in the chat group for the next shift
options.B: Call the hospital lawyer to prepare legal defense documents
options.C: Hide the empty medication wrapper in a pocket to destroy evidence
options.D: Assess the patient's clinical condition and provide any needed emergency care

explanation: The patient always comes first! Checking on their physical condition and providing any necessary care takes priority over paperwork and reporting.

question: Why must patients constantly rotate their injection sites?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing new syringes
options.B: To prevent localized skin hardening and altered drug absorption
options.C: To stop the needle from becoming dull during repeated use
options.D: To ensure the medication reaches the bloodstream much faster

explanation: Using the exact same spot over and over can cause fatty lumps (lipohypertrophy) and mess up how the drug is absorbed. Moving around keeps the skin healthy!

question: What dangerous event happens when severe swelling inside the skull pushes brain tissue downward?

options.A: Brain herniation
options.B: Ventriculomegaly
options.C: Cortical atrophy
options.D: Neural regeneration

explanation: Brain herniation is a medical emergency where high pressure forces brain tissue to shift where it shouldn't go. Keep up the good work!

question: When caring for someone at the end of life, who do we consider as the true unit of care?

options.A: The hospital ward staff
options.B: The dying patient alone
options.C: The entire family unit
options.D: The attending physician

explanation: In nursing, end-of-life care is never just about the patient alone. We look after the whole family because they share the emotional and psychological journey too!

question: Which of these is a classic, everyday cause of conductive hearing loss?

options.A: Presbycusis
options.B: Noise-induced hair cell damage
options.C: Cerumen impaction
options.D: Acoustic neuroma

explanation: Cerumen is just the medical term for earwax! When too much wax builds up and blocks the ear canal, sound waves can't reach the eardrum. A simple cleanup usually fixes it right up.

question: Why are mums who had a very long, exhausting labour at high risk of heavy bleeding after birth (PPH)?

options.A: Her exhausted uterine muscle fails to contract firmly to seal off bleeding blood vessels.
options.B: The placenta always remains completely attached inside the uterus forever.
options.C: Her body stops producing all platelets during the second stage of labour.
options.D: Her blood pressure naturally drops to zero immediately after delivery.

explanation: Correct! Think of the uterus like a muscle that just ran a marathon—by the end, it's too tired to clamp down tightly and shut off the bleeding vessels (uterine atony).

question: A patient comes to your clinic with severe watery diarrhea and dehydration after drinking untreated stream water. What condition should you suspect?

options.A: Cholera
options.B: Iron deficiency anemia
options.C: Hypertension
options.D: Rheumatoid arthritis

explanation: Spot on, nurse! Severe diarrhea and rapid fluid loss after drinking unsafe water are classic signs of a bacterial infection like cholera.

question: How do vitamins mostly help our bodies work?

options.A: Forming the primary structural skeleton of human bones
options.B: Serving as concentrated thermal insulation beneath the skin
options.C: Providing the bulk energy needed for intense physical exercise
options.D: Acting as coenzymes to help biochemical reactions run smoothly

explanation: Vitamins don't give you direct energy like carbs, but they act like little sparks or helpers (coenzymes) to keep your body's chemistry running smoothly.

question: What should you do immediately after using a needle to draw blood?

options.A: Carefully scoop the needle cap back on using one hand to prevent injury
options.B: Place the needle on a clean tray until the end of the shift
options.C: Break the needle tip off with forceps before throwing it in the bin
options.D: Drop the unrecapped needle directly into a puncture-resistant sharps container

explanation: Never recap needles! Dropping them straight into the sharps box right beside you is the safest way to avoid accidental needle-pricks.
